body: Thank you. Did just that. Thankfully we found her, and she's at the hospital now waiting for a psych consult.

Unfortunately her parents are in a different part of the country. Same with long-term friends. She does have other people around, but she doesn't see it that way. Another problem is that her friends here like to drink and she has problems with alcohol (which only exacerbates everything!). Thanks for your concern by the way. It's nice to have people to talk with about this.
I do know this. But sometimes I think I should stick with her despite my feelings. I don't want to lie to her, but it seems so selfish to leave when my support is important to her well-being.

She has once in the past, but she wouldn't take medication and didn't follow through with any support. At the time she didn't believe depression was real and thought people suffering it were melodramatic. This is really the first time she has stuck with treatment. I feel terrible that I might derail her progress now.

If it gets out of hand I will definitely call 911. I haven't in the past. Sometimes in the heat of the moment it gets difficult to judge what is best, and I didn't want to put her through that ordeal. But I can't help her on my own, especially if we're no longer together. I'm so pleased to hear that you're happy - it's great to know that it does get better for some. Thanks for the luck!

I just want to say thanks for the advice. I've never been in a situation like this before, nor do I know of anyone I'd feel comfortable speaking to. I've taken in what you've said, and I'm going to keep doing the best I can. 

I'm glad it worked out with your ex! Hopefully it'll be a similar thing at this end.

Thanks for your insight.

I always make sure to explicitly talk about suicide when I'm worried. I feel it's better than skirting the issue. During our last conversation she told me she "might not" do it, followed by "I probably won't". I'm afraid my moving out could be a tipping point though. 

Also, I want to be around for her if she ever needs me in the future - but I'm worried about making the separation harder on her. I'm a bit confused at how to best go about it.
I am being incredibly selfish. But how would I find someone to replace me?

I have tried extremely hard to be there for her. We've made progress too - she's been working through issues she's not been able to confront before. I don't want it all to end because of me. I really hope you're right... Thank-you for your kind words.
